guide.summary: A restored palace museum, a cultural institute, cooking schools, medina riad restaurants and Ville Nouvelle hotel bars, each checked against its own website.
highlights: Musée Al Batha des Arts de l'Islam
guide.tip: Musée Al Batha des Arts de l'Islam is closed on Tuesdays and Jnan L'Fassi at the Marriott is closed on Sundays, while Café Clock lists 9am to 11pm daily.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Musée Al Batha des Arts de l'Islam is closed on Tuesdays, and Jnan L'Fassi at the Fes Marriott Hotel Jnan Palace is closed on Sundays. Café Clock lists 9am to 11pm daily, and Eden at Palais Amani serves every day.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Musée Al Batha charges foreign visitors 60 DH, Moroccans 30 DH and children 15 DH, and the Fondation Nationale des Musées sells tickets online. A group cooking class at Café Clock costs 600 dh per person.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: La Dolce Vita at the Barceló says booking is required, Eden at Palais Amani says reservations are highly recommended, and Dar Roumana suggests booking ahead or at least at breakfast. Café Clock takes a non-refundable 50% deposit for cooking classes.

toolkit.label: Dress code
toolkit.copy: Riad Fès requires elegant attire in Gayza, the bar and on the Rooftop, with no flip-flops, football jerseys or large bags, and no shorts after 7pm except for children under 12. EME Lounge at the Marriott asks for smart casual.

guide.dek: Book medina dinners ahead, and keep your Musée Al Batha visit off Tuesdays.
intro: Start with the Musée Al Batha des Arts de l'Islam at 5 Place Batha. The Fondation Nationale des Musées says the palace reopened as a museum in February 2025 after restoration work that began in 2019. Its page lists 10:00 to 18:00 and says the museum is closed on Tuesdays. Tickets cost 60 DH for foreign visitors, 30 DH for Moroccans and 15 DH for children. For something current, the Institut français de Fès on Avenue Abou Obeida Ibn Al Jarrah shows the exhibition “Il était une fois un souk : Traversée intemporelle” from 18 October to 4 December 2026.

In the medina, Café Clock occupies a 250-year-old converted townhouse at 7 Derb El Magana, off Talaa Kbira, and its contact page lists 9am to 11pm daily. Its rooftop terrace looks across the medina to Mount Zalagh. You can book its traditional cooking class online: arrival is at 10:00, a market visit comes first, and the group price is 600 dh per person with a non-refundable 50% deposit. Fez Cooking School runs hands-on workshops at Palais Amani, 12 Derb El Miter, where Eden serves breakfast, lunch and dinner every day.

For a medina dinner, Gayza at Riad Fès serves lunch from 12:15 to 13:45 and dinner from 19:15 to 22:45 every day. Elegant attire is required there, in the bar and on the Rooftop, which looks over the medina to the mountains. Dar Roumana, at 30 Derb el Amer, opens from 7pm with last orders at 9:30pm, and three courses cost 440 dhs before 10% tax. If you are staying elsewhere, mention it when booking and a porter can meet you at the nearest medina gate.

In the Ville Nouvelle, the Barceló Fès Medina at 53 Avenue Hassan II runs La Dolce Vita, an Italian restaurant by chef Niki Pavanelli, open Monday to Saturday from 13:00 to 23:00, and booking is required. Its Cocoa Café serves coffee and snacks from 11:00 to 19:00. At the Fes Marriott Hotel Jnan Palace, 8 Avenue Ahmed Chaouki, Jnan L'Fassi pairs Moroccan food with live music from Monday to Saturday and is closed on Sundays. Croon Lounge serves cocktails and tapas from 7pm to 2am.
summaryCards: Pair the Musée Al Batha des Arts de l'Islam, closed on Tuesdays, with lunch or a cooking class at Café Clock on Derb El Magana.
Eden at Palais Amani serves breakfast from 7am to 10:30am every day, and Café Clock opens at 9am.
La Dolce Vita requires a reservation, Jnan L'Fassi is closed on Sundays and the Musée Al Batha is closed on Tuesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The Musée Al Batha page says both “Ouvert du lundi au dimanche” and “Fermé le mardi”; the guide follows the Tuesday closure. Opening hours were not published for L'Amandier, The Golden Bar, Amaraz, Restaurant La Maison Bleue, The Rooftop, the Palais Amani bar or Fez Cooking School, and Fez Café's and Karawan's restaurant pages returned 404, so their hours were not read. Café Clock and Dar Roumana showed no dated 2026 content, only current hours, prices and booking. The Musée Nejjarine site failed with a certificate error, a Riad Fès sub-page returned 403, and the Jnan Sbil PDF was too large to read. Bou Inania Madrasa, Al Quaraouiyine, the tanneries and Borj Nord had no official operator page with an address and hours, so they are left out. The Ruined Garden's and Nur's domains no longer show their restaurants. No bakery with an official page and Fès address was found, so the bakeries list is empty.
